standard_prerequisites.name: K-flat complexes and their homotopy invariance under the derived tensor product
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the property being established and the invariance that permits the replacement by F^bullet.

standard_prerequisites.name: Representation of a perfect object by a finite complex of finite projective modules, and homotopy equivalence of complexes of projectives that are isomorphic in the derived category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the finite complex F^bullet and the homotopy equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: The dual complex E^bullet of a finite complex of finite projectives and the identification of Hom with a total tensor complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Rewrites the Hom complex in the form to which the tensor-product K-flatness applies.

core_obligations: Record that the statement about representing R Hom_R(P^bullet, K^bullet) is the Hom-out-of-projective statement (proof line 28720).
Since P^bullet represents a perfect object, choose a finite complex F^bullet of finite projective R-modules isomorphic to P^bullet in D(R) (proof lines 28721-28724).

Use the description of maps from a projective complex to conclude that P^bullet and F^bullet are homotopy equivalent, hence that Hom^bullet(P^bullet, K^bullet) and Hom^bullet(F^bullet, K^bullet) are homotopy equivalent (proof lines 28725-28727).
Conclude that the first is K-flat exactly when the second is, using the definition of K-flatness and the homotopy invariance of the derived tensor product (proof lines 28728-28733).

Identify Hom^bullet(F^bullet, K^bullet) with the total complex Tot(E^bullet tensor_R K^bullet), where E^bullet is the dual complex with E^n = Hom_R(F^{-n}, R), by the dual-perfect-complex lemma and its proof (proof lines 28734-28742).
Conclude K-flatness: E^bullet is a bounded complex of projectives hence K-flat, and the tensor product of K-flat complexes is K-flat (proof lines 28743-28745).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a bounded above complex P^bullet of projective R-modules, and a K-flat complex K^bullet of R-modules, and asserts that if P^bullet represents a perfect object of D(R) then Hom^bullet(P^bullet, K^bullet) is K-flat and represents R Hom_R(P^bullet, K^bullet) (source lines 28710-28717). The second assertion is immediate from the Hom-out-of-projective statement (proof line 28720). The substantive part is the K-flatness. Since P^bullet represents a perfect object, the proof chooses a finite complex F^bullet of finite projective R-modules isomorphic to it in D(R) (proof lines 28721-28724). Because both are complexes of projectives, they are in fact homotopy equivalent, by the description of maps from a projective complex, so Hom^bullet(P^bullet, K^bullet) and Hom^bullet(F^bullet, K^bullet) are homotopy equivalent, and hence the first is K-flat exactly when the second is, using the definition of K-flatness and the homotopy-invariance of derived tensor product (proof lines 28725-28733). The proof then computes Hom^bullet(F^bullet, K^bullet) as the total complex Tot(E^bullet tensor_R K^bullet), where E^bullet is the dual complex of F^bullet with terms E^n = Hom_R(F^{-n}, R), using the dual-perfect-complex lemma and its proof (proof lines 28734-28742). Finally, since E^bullet is a bounded complex of projectives it is K-flat, and the tensor product of K-flat complexes is K-flat, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 28743-28745). The non-routine content is the replacement of P^bullet by the finite complex F^bullet together with the identification of the Hom complex with a tensor product of the dual complex.
